Title: Simple Cardboard Invention May Help Billions
Content: Not every useful invention has to be developed over many `text(years)` and cost a lot of money to make. Sometimes the simplest of ideas can improve our lives profoundly. All it takes is a little imagination and a desire to make a difference!

Ask John Bohmer, whose weekend project with his `text(two)` daughters may end up not only make a significant difference in helping our environment but also improving the lives of `text(3 billion)` people worldwide.

John's invention is a solar-powered oven made from cardboard. Dubbed¹ Kyoto Box, it is composed of `text(two)` cardboard boxes, `text(one)` inside the other, covered with a sheet of acrylic glass - to help trap the heat from the sun. The inner box is painted with black paint, which absorbs the heat, while the box on the outside is lined with silver foil that reflects any energy that escapes toward the black box. This helps to create a concentrated source of energy that can be used for cooking.

The simple oven costs only `text($7 USD)` to manufacture² and can easily be put together in any cardboard factory. With the capability of reaching high temperatures, it can be used to boil water, cook rice and casserole - and even bake bread.

It is estimated that over `text(3 billion)` people living in developing countries use chopped firewood for their main fuel, generating an estimated `text(2 tons)` of dangerous carbon dioxide emissions a `text(year)`.
While solar cookers are not a new idea, this is the `text(first)` time someone has come up with `text(one)` that works and is cheap enough to be adapted on a large scale.
